subject: HelixCommerce: sudden 502s & token latency — urgent network path review
messages:
From: Susan Li <susan.li@helixcommerce.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: ops@helixcommerce.com
Date: 2027-08-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production: sudden 502s + elevated token latency since 08:50

Hi Monica,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 502s and token-generation latency for our /generate endpoint around 08:50 PDT. Error rate is ~6-8% for the last 15 minutes; end-to-end p95 latency jumped from 180ms to 1.9s and throughput dropped ~25%.

We traced a couple of request IDs (trace-id: hxc-7f2a1, hxc-7f2a8) and attached a small pcap + application logs that show a mix of SYN retries and some RSTs when our requests hit Redwood egress.

We had a routine peering maintenance earlier this morning in our account (nothing on our side after 07:00) but the timing looks coincident. Can we get an urgent ops call with networking/SRE to confirm if there's a VPC peering route flap, firewall/proxy changes, or DNS misrouting? This is impacting checkout flows — customers are seeing timeouts.

Attachments: pcap-snippet.txt, trace-logs-7f2a.zip (referenced in log)

— Susan
Susan Li
VP, Infrastructure & Ops
HelixCommerce
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Susan Li <susan.li@helixcommerce.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-09T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 502s + elevated token latency since 08:50

Susan — thanks for the quick heads-up and the artifacts. I'm pulling in our network and SRE leads (cc'd). We can join a call in ~15 minutes.

Immediate asks before we join:
- Can you share a couple of full trace ids (app-level) for failed requests?
- Any changes to your peering config or firewall rules this morning?
- Confirm whether the failures are all hitting a single Redwood region (us-west-2) or multiple.

We'll prioritize a mitigation path (temporary traffic shift or bypass) while we triage. I'll update in the call and post runbook steps after.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-09T09:25:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Production: sudden 502s + elevated token latency since 08:50

Team — forwarding Helix's report. Key items from their artifacts: SYN retries, some RSTs, and elevated retransmits at the egress hop.

Initial internal notes (please act, prioritized):
- Check egress NAT/conntrack counters on the region serving Helix (us-west-2); look for conntrack table exhaustion or rapid timeout churn.
- Confirm recent peering table changes or route refresh events around 07:30–09:00. (Helix reported maintenance earlier.)
- Run tcpdump on the egress interface and collect first-hop traces (capture attached: helix_first_hop_traces.txt).
- Review our proxy/firewall layer metrics for queueing/backpressure and any config rollouts in the last 6 hours.
- Validate DNS resolution patterns for helixcommerce endpoints — check TTLs and if we returned an unexpected CNAME/regional endpoint.

I'm starting a short mitigation plan we can enact in <30m: (a) fail traffic to alternate peering if available; (b) temporarily route Helix through dedicated direct pool bypassing proxy layer; (c) increase conntrack table sizes if we see exhaustion.

Attaching current triage runbook: runbook_network_triage.md

— Monica
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-09T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: sudden 502s + elevated token latency since 08:50

Seeing the same signal on our telemetry — a spike in TCP retransmits and a jump in SYN->SYN-ACK timeouts on the primary egress. Our edge peering fabric recorded route updates at 07:37 UTC which correlate to the customer's window.

Immediate actions taken (done):
- Opened SUP-3489 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3489) and attached the captures.
- Initiated traffic shift for HelixCommerce to alternate peering path in us-west-2 (takes <90s to propagate); early tests show p95 latency falling back toward baseline and 502s dropping to ~0.5%.
- Notified SRE to increase conntrack max and to watch for table churn; will revert if no impact.

Notes / hypothesis:
- Likely root cause: peering route flaps combined with our proxy layer exposing short-lived NAT sessions (conntrack) — packet reordering and retry storms push some flows into RST territory.
- DNS inconsistent resolution could exacerbate path mixing; we should audit TTLs and resolve times for helix endpoints.

Requesting: Vivek to approve a short executive notification if impact persists >30m so we can offer credits and escalate contract SLA if required.

— Rishi
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Susan Li <susan.li@helixcommerce.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@helixcommerce.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-09T10:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sudden 502s + elevated token latency since 08:50

Monica / Rishi — thanks for the rapid response and the traffic shift. We validated a quick A/B: traffic over the alternate peering path reduced p95 to ~210ms and 502s to near zero for a 30-minute window.

A few asks to close the loop:
1) Can we get a permanent remediation plan? We need root-cause analysis (peering vs our proxy config) and a timeline for the fix.
2) We will need an executive-level update + credit conversation given this impacted checkout during a peak window. Please loop in Redwood finance/execs.
3) Please share final captures and the SUP-3489 ticket when available (we attached a small pcap-snippet for your reference).

We'll keep monitoring but would like an ETA for a full RCA and a patch schedule.

— Susan
Susan Li
VP, Infrastructure & Ops
HelixCommerce
